scope: Evidence-backed dispositions over the measured instance mapping; recommendations do not create correspondence credit or approve unresolved policy changes

decisions.title: Existing corresponding check
decisions.recommendation: No rule change for this observed pairing; retain compliant and violating controls.

decisions.title: Worthwhile request traversal gap
decisions.recommendation: Enumerate getArmResourceOperationList for each already-registered resource; select createOrUpdate PUTs, reuse the existing request predicate and deduplicate Operation targets. This avoids a broad PUT listener and shared registry redesign. The probe verifies reachability and the canonical selected response, not post-fix warning counts.

decisions.title: Custom lifecycle registration/modeling gap
decisions.recommendation: The PUT is absent from every registered resource's operation Set, despite a registered selected response. Review the low-level/custom template or its resource argument before adding explicit lifecycle registration. Verify emitted paths, operation IDs and wire schemas do not change; do not infer a canonical model from HTTP PUT alone.

decisions.title: Confirmed Swagger false positive
decisions.recommendation: Identical 200/201 references were compared by resolved JavaScript object identity. Do not reproduce this bug or count its absence as a missing useful diagnostic.

decisions.title: Genuine schema difference with an existing native owner
decisions.recommendation: Quota deliberately models a quota resource at 200 and a submission-status envelope at 201. Azure Core response-schema-problem already compares non-error success payload identities; the source explicitly suppresses it. Use that owner and review the legacy-contract exception instead of adding a duplicate ARM warning. The final LRO result is separately modeled as the quota resource; initial-envelope and final-result policies are different.

decisions.title: Missing independent response-resource policy
decisions.recommendation: The selected emitted hierarchy lacks x-ms-azure-resource, and its source payload is not a registered ARM resource. This is unimplemented policy, not proof that all instances are legitimate resource-contract bugs. Prefer a focused source-level response-resource check after defining custom/action exceptions; account for emitter marker state, custom-resource options, explicit extensions and external references. Do not overload canonical-resource identity or add emitted-JSON equality.

decisions.title: Empty 200: real response-body issue, not two unequal payload models
decisions.recommendation: Keep schema consistency separate from response existence. Review no-response-body and authored suppressions, and repair the spec only against the actual wire contract. Its current implementation checks the first ordinary response and skips some template operations; source ownership alone is not measured coverage. The focused owner-predicate results are linked in gap-analysis.md.

decisions.title: Swagger schema-comparison false positive / policy overreach
decisions.recommendation: The comparison treats a correctly bodyless 202 or 204 as an unequal resource schema. Do not invent a response body or add a resource-schema warning merely to match that result. This does not establish that the operation's status set is ARM-compliant: arm-put-response-codes owns that separate question. This is a recommended intentional difference, not approved retirement or existing migration credit.

decisions.title: Swagger collection-shape comparison false positive
decisions.recommendation: The compared payloads are an entity/array/list-envelope role difference, not evidence of different resource item models. The saved schemas show matching item identity. Keep list envelope/item validation separate; do not compare wrapper reference names across collection and item-like methods. This recommendation is not approved retirement or existing migration credit.

decisions.title: Bulk/collection request contract, not ordinary resource replacement
decisions.recommendation: Annotations creates an item but returns an array; FirewallRules_Replace supplies a list to a collection operation. These shapes are not automatically equivalent, but HTTP PUT alone does not establish a single-resource replacement contract. Require spec-owner intent before extending the canonical-resource rule; do not claim these are confirmed compliant APIs.

decisions.title: Action-like PUT contract
decisions.recommendation: Gateway API association and storage migration use command/association inputs rather than the parent resource model. GatewayApi is registered as action, has a different ApiContract response and explicitly suppresses the current ARM rule. Do not compare its input to the Gateway parent simply because its verb is PUT. Review API design and justified exceptions separately rather than widening this resource listener.

decisions.title: Unregistered body-bearing request/response mismatch
decisions.recommendation: The differing request and response are observable, but no registered canonical resource is established. ExportConfiguration, TestJob, SyncJob, ConnectionMonitor and PacketCapture need owner review of read-only fields, visibility and actual contract before a modeling repair. These are five checked PUTs, not their repeated raw finding total. Do not add a generic recursive schema comparator for these legacy DTOs.

decisions.title: Canonical parent differs from the actual child response
decisions.recommendation: ApiManagement PrivateEndpointConnection uses ApiManagementServiceResource as the legacy resource argument; RecoveryServices certificate uses Vault but returns VaultCertificateResponse. Existing request warnings compare to the parent, not the original selected child response. Review child-resource/custom-operation modeling and preserve wire behavior; an extra equality warning is not the first fix.

decisions.title: Genuine PUT/GET resource-shape difference
decisions.priority: P3: spec-owner follow-up; defer broad matcher
decisions.recommendation: SyncJob's PUT response has read-only name/type/id; GET has writable id, omits name/type, and adds nested exception. These are not merely differently named aliases. Establish whether the wire contract should share a model; do not rewrite the spec if the service intentionally returns a summary versus detail. One observed route does not justify a general recursive, version/visibility-aware cross-operation structural comparator.
